object_description: flat building covering the whole plot, with a two-storey attic volume set on the roof
geometry_property: one upper floor plus accessible roof
roof enclosed by a ball catcher
split into two wings by a central passage
design_condition: the building occupies the entire plot and gives the square its spatial conclusion to the north, staying low against the much taller surroundings and lifting the outdoor space onto the roof

positive: The building gives the square its spatial conclusion to the north
Staying flat sets the school apart from the much taller surroundings and reveals its public character
The outdoor space with pitch and break area is consistently arranged on the roof
Residents can reach the roof via stairs in the open, continuous entrance hall without entering the school
Each school wing has a central, spacious staircase
The base of the footbridge stairs lies at the level of the central entrance hall, making the daytime connection to the square a matter of course
All special rooms are arranged at ground level with four identical clusters above
The clear urban planning approach and the rich facade with a lively interplay of light and shadow make the project attractive
negative: The two-storey attic kindergarten does not appear to belong to the building and could read as a later addition
The central access divides the building into two halves, limiting operational flexibility
Folding doors can close the hall at night, so the pitch is not necessarily available to residents outside school hours
The roof and footbridge connections depend on the passageway not being blocked
Because the clusters lie along the central route, the special education school cannot be separated
The group rooms are too narrow and the front zones too large
Load-bearing interior walls contradict the intention of adapting to changing needs, so flexibility is low
Access to the gymnasium outside school hours is unresolved
The kindergarten layout is not ideal, with rooms too narrow and corridors too large
The access area is too large and requires higher investment costs
The photovoltaic placement is only mentioned in passing and infiltration is not addressed
Reservations remain about the organisation of the school programme and about economic efficiency
